This is the linear map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the space of continuous linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that sends $a$ to the…
nodes.title: The $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing as a linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the continuous linear functional $x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the space of sequences $\iota \to \mathbb{K}$ tending to $0$ at infinity with the supremum norm, has operator norm equal to $\|a\|_1 = \sum_{i \in \iota} |a_i|$.
nodes.title: The $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing is isometric

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type, and for $i \in \iota$ let $e_i \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then the functional $x \mapsto \sum_{j \in \iota} (e_i)_j x_j$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ given by pairing with $e_i$ is the evaluation $x \mapsto x_i$ at $i$.
nodes.title: Pairing with a unit vector is evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type. For every continuous linear functional $\varphi$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ there is $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with $\varphi(x) = \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$ for all $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$; that is, the pairing map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the continuous dual of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ is surjective.
nodes.title: Every functional on $c_0$ comes from $\ell^1$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type. The pairing is the continuous linear map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the continuous dual of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that sends $a$ to the functional $x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$.
nodes.title: The $\ell^1$–$c_0$ duality pairing

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type. For $i \in \iota$, evaluation at $i$ is the continuous linear functional $x \mapsto x_i$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Coordinate evaluation on $c_0$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type, and let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For every continuous linear functional $\varphi$ on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, every finite set $s \subseteq \iota$ and every $c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$, we have $\varphi(\sum_{i \in s} c_i e_i) = \sum_{i \in s} c_i \, \varphi(e_i)$.
nodes.title: A functional on a finitely supported sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type, and let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For every finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, every $c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ and every $j \in \iota$, the $j$-th coordinate of $\sum_{i \in s} c_i e_i$ is $c_j$ if $j \in s$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Coordinates of a finitely supported sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type, and let $e_i \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. For a finite set $s \subseteq \iota$ and $c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$, the finitely supported sequence with coefficients $c$ on $s$ is the element $\sum_{i \in s} c_i e_i$ of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Finitely supported sequences in $c_0$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type. The map that sends $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the same sequence $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$, viewed in the subspace of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ of sequences tending to $0$ along the cofinite filter, is a linear isometric equivalence onto that subspace.
nodes.title: $c_0$ is isometrically isomorphic to the null sequences in $\ell^\infty$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the real or complex field and $\iota$ an index type. For every $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the norm of $x$ equals the norm $\sup_{i \in \iota} |x_i|$ of $x$ viewed as an element of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The $c_0$ norm is the supremum norm

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. A bounded sequence $x \in \ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose coordinates $x_i$ tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$ defines the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with the same coordinates.
nodes.title: Sequences in $\ell^\infty$ tending to zero as elements of $c_0$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the linear functional on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ given by pairing with $a$ takes the value $\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$ at $x$.
nodes.title: Value of the functional of an $\ell^1$ sequence on $c_0$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, this is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K}) \to \mathbb{K}$ sending $x$ to $\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$.
nodes.title: Pairing with an $\ell^1$ sequence as a linear functional on $c_0$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For indices $i, j \in \iota$ and $a \in \mathbb{K}$, the $j$-th coordinate of the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that is $a$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere equals $a$ if $j = i$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the sequence supported at one index

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For $i \in \iota$ and $a \in \mathbb{K}$, the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that is $a$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere has norm $\|a\|$.
nodes.title: Norm of a sequence supported at one index

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For an index $i \in \iota$ and a scalar $a \in \mathbb{K}$, this is the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $a$ and whose other coordinates are $0$.
nodes.title: Sequence supported at one index

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. The sequences $x \in \ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose coordinates $x_i$ tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$ form a $\mathbb{K}$-linear subspace of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The subspace of null sequences in $\ell^\infty$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be an index type, and let $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of functions $\iota \to \mathbb{K}$ vanishing at infinity for the discrete topology on $\iota$. For every $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the coordinates $x_i$ tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$.
nodes.title: Elements of $c_0$ tend to zero along the cofinite filter

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. Every $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ is a bounded sequence, and this map sends it to the element of $\ell^\infty(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with the same coordinates $x_i$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of $c_0$ in $\ell^\infty$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be an index type. For a finite set $s \subseteq \iota$, an element $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and an index $j \in \iota$, the $j$-th coordinate of the truncation of $x$ to $s$ equals $x_j$ if $j \in s$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Coordinates of a finite truncation

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type, let $s \subseteq \iota$ be a finite set and let $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. The truncation of $x$ to $s$ is the element of $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose $j$-th coordinate is $x_j$ for $j \in s$ and $0$ for $j \notin s$; it is defined as $\sum_{i \in s} x_i e_i$, where $e_i$ is the sequence that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere.
nodes.title: Finite truncation of a $c_0$ sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $w \in \mathbb{K}$, the normalizing scalar $u(w)$ of $w$, which is $0$ if $w = 0$ and $\overline{w}/|w|$ otherwise, satisfies $u(w)\, w = |w|$, with $|w|$ regarded as an element of $\mathbb{K}$.
nodes.title: The normalizing scalar times $w$ is $|w|$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For $w \in \mathbb{K}$, the normalizing scalar $u(w) \in \mathbb{K}$ of $w$ is $0$ if $w = 0$ and $\overline{w}/|w|$ otherwise, so that $u(w)\, w = |w|$.
nodes.title: The normalizing scalar $\overline{w}/|w|$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be a type. The space $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ consists of the functions $x : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ that tend to $0$ along the cofinite filter, that is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the set $\{i : |x_i| \ge \varepsilon\}$ is finite, with pointwise operations and the supremum norm $\|x\|_\infty = \sup_i |x_i|$. It is realized as the space of continuous…

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type and let $\Phi$ be a continuous linear functional on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. For $i \in \iota$ let $e_i$ be the sequence that is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. The coefficient sequence $(\Phi(e_i))_{i \in \iota}$, as an element of $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, has norm $\sum_{i \in \iota} |\Phi(e_i)|$ at most the operator norm $\|\Phi\|$.
nodes.title: $\ell^1$ norm of the coefficients of a functional on $c_0$

For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $a$ under the continuous linear pairing map $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K}) \to c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})^*$, which is the…
nodes.title: The pairing map $\ell^1 \to c_0^*$ does not increase norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be a type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $a$ under the linear pairing map from $\ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ to the continuous linear functionals on $c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, which is the functional $x \mapsto \sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i$, has operator norm at most $\|a\|_1 = \sum_i |a_i|$.
nodes.title: Norm bound for the functional of an $\ell^1$ sequence on $c_0$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be a type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, $|\sum_{i \in \iota} a_i x_i| \le \|a\|_1 \|x\|_\infty$, where $\|a\|_1 = \sum_i |a_i|$ and $\|x\|_\infty = \sup_i |x_i|$.
nodes.title: Bound for the $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $w \in \mathbb{K}$, the normalizing scalar $u(w)$ of $w$, which is $0$ if $w = 0$ and $\overline{w}/|w|$ otherwise, satisfies $|u(w)| \le 1$.
nodes.title: The normalizing scalar has absolute value at most one

nodes.summary: The pairing has operator norm at most one.
nodes.title: Duality pairing has operator norm at most one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be a type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and $x \in c_0(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the family $(a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is (unconditionally) summable.
nodes.title: Summability of the $\ell^1$–$c_0$ pairing

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be any index type. For every $a \in \ell^1(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, the family of norms $(\|a_i\|)_{i \in \iota}$ is summable.
nodes.title: Coordinate norms of an $\ell^1$ family are summable
Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
